The CONTROL device formulation employs MACl at 0.3 mg/mL in the perovskite precursor solution, which aids crystallization but fails to adequately suppress interfacial and bulk defects. This limitation manifests in a relatively low open-circuit voltage (Voc = 1.0304 V) and short-circuit current density (Jsc = 20.871 mA/cm²), indicating significant non-radiative recombination and suboptimal charge extraction. The methylammonium cation in MACl is volatile and provides only transient passivation, leaving grain boundaries and surfaces vulnerable to trap states that accelerate carrier recombination and ion migration. Consequently, the fill factor (FF = 73.822%) is constrained by resistive losses and interfacial barriers, limiting the power conversion efficiency (PCE = 15.876%). PMACl, absent in the CONTROL formulation, offers a superior alternative due to its bulky phenethylammonium cation, which forms a thin, stable 2D perovskite layer atop the 3D bulk. This layer passivates undercoordinated lead ions and halide vacancies at grain boundaries and interfaces, directly reducing trap-assisted recombination and suppressing ion migration. The enhanced defect passivation elevates Voc by minimizing voltage losses, while the improved film morphology and crystallinity facilitate efficient charge transport, boosting Jsc. Although the insulating nature of the 2D layer could theoretically impede vertical conductivity, the low concentration (0.3 mg/mL) ensures a conformal monolayer that balances passivation with minimal series resistance, preserving FF. Replacing MACl with PMACl at an identical concentration (0.3 mg/mL) thus addresses the core limitations of the CONTROL device without introducing processing complexity. The optimized formulation is expected to achieve a Voc between 1.073 V and 1.113 V, a Jsc between 23.62 mA/cm² and 24.02 mA/cm², an FF between 73.51% and 75.51%, and a PCE between 18.63% and 20.19%.
